recipes.name: Awesome Ham Pasta Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 large red bell pepper, cut into 1 inch pieces
1 large green bell pepper, cut into 1 inch pieces
15 small sweet pickles, chopped, juice reserved

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain.
In a large bowl, mix together the drained pasta, ham, peppers, onion, pickles and tomatoes.

In a small bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, sour cream, beef bouillon granules, vinegar, salt, pepper, garlic and 1/2 cup of reserved pickle juice. Fold into the salad and toss gently until evenly coated. Chill overnight to allow the flavors to blend. Serve near room temperature.

raw_recipe.headline: Awesome Ham Pasta Salad
raw_recipe.description: This ham and ziti pasta salad is perked up with colorful bell peppers, red onion, sweet pickles and cherry tomatoes. It’s tossed with a sweet and tangy dressing.

review.reviewBody: WOW!!!! What a really good recipe!! I always thought I made a mean pasta salad, but this recipe makes me want to chuck mine out the window! While I wouldn't recommend changing a thing, I did try adding a couple of things that might be worth your time trying: cubed cucumbers, sliced black olives, and different colored sweet peppers. Something to note as well: when you first make this salad, it almost appears as if there might be too much dressing. If you chill it overnight, or even for a few hours, the dressing homogenizes itself and you have just the right amount. Thank you, Karena, for this great recipe!

I have made this at least ten times. We love it! It's a great make-ahead dish. I did make a few changes. The dressing is very rich. I compensate by adding an orange bell pepper, way more tomatoes, and a little extra pasta. I'm happy to use three or more cups of tomatoes. The chopping does take awhile, but it is a large batch of pasta salad that keeps for days. To speed things up, I spin the tomatoes in a salad spinner to get the seeds out, use a chopper for the peppers, and grate the onion.

Loved this. Even my husband who generally dislikes pasta salad enjoyed it. (I admit I picked it hoping he would.) What really excites me is that my family usually doesn't like sweet pickles, and also won't eat tomatoes. I made it the 2nd time using greek yogurt instead of sour cream and light mayo. I put half the sweet pickle juice because light mayo always seems sweeter? I should add that I don't have beef bouillion granules, I mixed in the equivalent amount of beef better than bouillion right after the pasta was strained.

Thank you Karena for a great recipe! You're right about its popularity! This recipe makes a ton! The only things i might change are: Less red onion or use a sweeter variety like a peruvian red or vadalia or even to switch it up, green onion in place of it. I used bread and butter pickles, and 3/4 of the mayo called for. If anyone doesnt like the acrid taste of the onion, but still wants to include it, just chop it coarsly like the recipe but before adding to all the ingredients put in a bowl with a fat pinch of salt, stir and let it sit for 15-30mins, then rinse and taste then add to the salad.

I have made this recipe many times and it is truly awesome and so flexible and forgiving with substitutions. I've made it exactly as written and it's great but you can add in lots of other stuff based on your family's preference. We like to add broccoli, cheddar cubes, fresh or canned pineapple, cherry tomatoes. I also use sweet green pickle relish instead of sweet pickles because that's what I always have on hand. I've also subbed bouillion powder with liquid beef bouillon and it turns out just fine. I always plan on extra ham just so I can make this salad. Thanks Karena for a great recipe!

I couldn't even wait for this to chill in the fridge overnight- grabbed a bowl and already chowed some down. How could this possibly taste better tomorrow? Seriously? It's already delicious AS IS, just after mixing it! Best pasta salad I have ever had! I did not add the peppers only because no one in the family likes them but me. Might add some another time in a small bowl just for me only, but I don't know if this salad even needs them! 

Also, you can buy some brown sugar ham cut one inch thick at the deli counter, for those who would love to make this without having to cook an entire ham. That's what I did, and thank goodness I bought two one inch slices (approximately two pounds worth of brown sugar ham, mmmmmmm mmmm!!!!)instead of one, as I made a double batch of this with double the pasta (total of 32 oz of cavatappi pasta cooked. 

Sorry to the other viewers who used the sweet pickle relish, but I preferred to use the sweet pickles in the original recipe with a half of a cup of pickle juice (1/4 of a cup if you make a singular batch). I'm not so sure I'd want to use the sweet relish after eating this with the sweet pickles and their juice!

Anyhow, thanks for a fabulous recipe- I already know it's going to be hit tomorrow night with my family! All ham and pickle lovers, and both in a pasta salad? Who could beat that? Oh, and the beef bouillon granules (I used no sodium granules) tasted fabulous in this- however did you come up with this idea?

I just made this recipe and think it is very good, but I find it to be a bit too salty, even after setting overnight. Ham, beef bouillon, and mayonnaise all are salty to begin with. I don't see a reason to add an additional half teaspoon of salt. I am wondering whether using equal amounts of sour cream with the mayo also would help curtail the salt.

I made it with mini farfalle instead of ziti, and that worked just fine. I like garlic, but I tried the option without. I also added some green peas to one serving and liked them, so I might add a bag to the mix the next time I make this.

If the original recipe is supposed to make six servings, they must be huge servings, because this made a LOT of salad! I made this as a trial run for serving a crowd, and I'm glad I did, because I probably will prepare for fewer servings. I scooped out at least 10 8-ounce measuring cups of salad from this single recipe.
I made it with rotini pasta and only 1 pepper, 1/2 lb. ham, and 1/2 c. chopped sweet pickles in juice. It made over 3.5 pounds! Would cut back a little on the mayo/sour cream sauce.

This is a new favorite I used a 12 ounce box of whole wheat rotini, and a little extra mayo/sour cream. I only had two beef bouillon cubes, so I let them soak in the vinegar and then mushed them up into a liquid before adding to mayo mixture. I only chilled it for about an hour before serving, and it was still awesome, can't wait to have the little bit of leftover tomorrow. Looking forward to playing around with additions such as peas. Thank you for this new favorite!

I used two very large red bell peppers (instead of one red, one green) and I used equal amounts garlic dill pickles instead of sweet pickles. To the dressing, I added a few spices (onion powder, garlic powder, dried dill weed, fresh ground pepper, a little hot sauce). I did not add the full amount of dill pickle juice, I just kept adding until it was the consistancy I was looking for. This makes an excellent quick lunch--I mixed it up the night before and portioned it out into small Tupperware containers (my husband took two!)--with a homemade yeast roll. Very filling. Adding additional spices really made this salad great. I did miss the addition of hard boiled eggs, I will make this again but add in a couple chopped hard boiled eggs.

We really enjoyed this. I used regular macaroni, green onions, better than bouillon because that is what I had on hand. I think this would be good using sea shell macaroni. Just chop your vegetables to go with the size of the macaroni you're using. Definitely will be making this one again. Thank you for the great recipe.
Add some chopped cucumbers and cheddar cheese.
Ham salads are inexplicably underappreciated. This one looks good - and with pasta as a bonus. Dinner tonight!

I've made this salad in the past, and under a different name. For a full-on Italian flavor, I've added ham, salami, pepperoni and olives, both black and green. This one was a mini version of my other, so YES, it's a keeper. (On a side note, I buy those pre-cut onions and pepper medley. It works for me)
Easy & tasty
I love this salad!!! I made it exactly as specified in the recipe and, WOW! This is going to be a summer favorite for sure♥️♥️♥️

It IS awesome! Couldn't wait till it chilled overnight. It is delicious right now, and I can't wait to try it tomorrow. I didn't add cherry tomatoes because their cost was totally prohibitive in our grocery store this week. I would love to try this in the summer with chunks of grilled chicken instead of the ham. This will be a regular. Thanks for the recipe!
Awesome recipe that’s just a little different than the standard boring pasta salads. Definitely a keeper recipe
My husband and I loved it and he wanted to eat it for breakfast the next morning. This recipe will definitely become part of my summer meals rotation.

Delicious! Made it vegetarian by using fake plant based “bacon” and vegan Mayo. At first it was swimming in dressing. The next morning all the dressing had absorbed. If I’d make it again I’d probably do 1.5 times dressing so it’s a bit creamier. Even the meat lovers loved it. Just didn’t tell them it wasn’t real ham!!!
